memory_candidates.title: proof_wanted is invisible to both a sorry-grep and #print axioms
memory_candidates.content: In Lean/Mathlib-style libraries, `proof_wanted` declares a statement WITHOUT adding any declaration to the environment. A `grep -c sorry` returns 0 and `#print axioms` reports a clean profile for everything that does not depend on it, so neither detects it. In cslib's omega-automata tree all 54 files had 0 sorries while 8 main theorems (including the whole correctness of its Buchi complementation construction) were proof_wanted. The check that settles it is an environment-presence probe: `run_cmd do let env <- Lean.getEnv; ... (env.find? `Ns.thm).isSome` — remembering to import the module that should define it, or the probe returns a false negative of its own.

memory_candidates.title: Assess an external Lean library as a port by measuring its Mathlib rev skew first
memory_candidates.content: Before costing a port from another Lean repo, check whether the dependency's pinned Mathlib HEAD is itself a renaming/refactor commit. cslib pinned Mathlib 169c26b5, whose commit subject is literally 'refactor: rename restrict to domRestrict (#25980)', 76 commits ahead of the consuming tree — and the first line of the first ported proof failed with invalidField on exactly that rename, despite both repos sharing an identical lean-toolchain. An identical toolchain does NOT imply pin-neutral ports. Cost the transitive import closure too: one 147-line leaf theorem was cheap, but the library's headline result pulled 47 modules / 7,526 lines.

memory_candidates.title: Audit a literature sub-index for author-year stem collisions, not just orphans
memory_candidates.content: Corpus ids must be matched whole, but nothing detects NEW stem collisions. Grouping sub-index doc_ids by author-year stem and flagging groups whose members lack a `hazard` while their global provenance_fidelity values differ found three unrecorded collisions in one pass, one of them (vardi_1996_automata_ltl, verified_conversion, vs vardi_1996_automata-theoretic-ltl, no_source_pdf) with opposite fidelity verdicts — exactly the failure the ids-matched-whole convention exists to prevent. Orphan checks pass cleanly while this is wrong.
